stances.reasoning: In a 2019 op-ed Driscoll listed 'expand access to reproductive care' among her core Democratic priorities, and she ran on the 2022 Healey-Driscoll ticket whose signature issue was protecting abortion access at all stages in Massachusetts. As Lt. Governor she serves in the first administration of an openly gay governor and has consistently supported anti-discrimination policies and equity initiatives.

In a 2019 op-ed she called for 'bold, state leadership' on climate and supported a carbon fee on fossil fuels. Her approach is investing in clean energy and gradually reducing fossil fuel use — short of an emergency declaration or hard 2030 deadline.

As Salem mayor Driscoll established Salem as a sanctuary city. During the 2023 shelter crisis she described migrants as 'fleeing horrific circumstances,' called it 'a humanitarian crisis,' and pushed for federal work authorization for immigrants rather than removal. Her public framing consistently opposes deportation of people without violent criminal histories and focuses on providing services and legal pathways.

In a 2019 op-ed co-authored with Mayor Alex Morse, Driscoll explicitly supported legislation placing a carbon fee on 'gas, oil, and coal' to make 'dirty energy becomes more expensive' and encourage transition away from fossil fuels. She called for state leadership to stop new fossil fuel reliance and invest in renewable alternatives. This aligns with stopping new fossil fuel permits rather than expanding drilling.

Driscoll as Lt. Governor oversaw the 2023 migrant shelter crisis, stating the state was 'really running out of capacity' and advocating for new congregate shelters and federal work authorization for immigrants. She declined to call for eliminating the right-to-shelter law. Her approach prioritized expanding shelter capacity and services over criminalization, consistent with decriminalizing public sleeping while investing in shelter.

As Lt. Governor, Driscoll led the working group establishing the independent Executive Office of Housing and Livable Communities and described her goal as a 'housing moonshot' to close a 200,000-unit gap. She links housing investment to transit access and has championed public funding for affordable housing. This reflects a rent-caps-plus-public-funding approach rather than pure market deregulation.

Her record consistently supports keeping legal immigration open and providing services regardless of status.

Governor with Maura Healey — the first openly lesbian governor — on a ticket that explicitly championed LGBTQ+ rights and marriage equality. Salem under her leadership celebrated LGBTQ+ Pride and the Healey-Driscoll administration has signed shield laws protecting same-sex couples and transgender individuals from out-of-state interference.

She engaged in voter registration outreach with homeless residents at Pine Street Inn in September 2024, emphasizing that all eligible voters' voices matter. Her alignment with the Healey administration's support for expanded mail-in voting and early voting access in Massachusetts further supports this stance.
